title: Independent verification: integral-divisibility kernel replay and radix 81
body:
## Result and scope

**Independent verification / research note; no new kappa.** This corroborates
Hao Yan's concurrent [PR 796](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/796) and Ali Romman's incorporated [PR 621](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/621) using a different
valuation-extraction method: repeated exact integral division by `pi=1-u`.
It also adds every primitive embedding at radix 81, beyond [PR 796](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/796)'s cutoff of 68.
The shared Newton-polygon formula is credited to the concurrent contribution;
no mathematical priority or new archimedean conditioning bound is claimed.

The standalone integer engine reconstructs actual tail-product coefficients,
checks the shifted cyclotomic polynomial is Eisenstein, and compares three
obligations: weighted-basis minima, exact integral-divisibility counts, and
the factor-valuation sum. An integer convex hull is checked against the rational
segment formula. No predecessor field/SymPy/determinant code is imported.

- Complete fixed domain: 13 radices, **214 primitive embeddings / 10,268 exact
  coefficients**, with eight rejection controls and per-embedding coefficient hashes.
- Pinned [PR 796](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/796) receipt comparison: all twelve shared radices, **160 embeddings /
  5,894 coefficient obligations**, hulls and root multiplicities agree.
- Additional radix 81: **54 embeddings / 4,374 coefficients**, checked by both
  extraction methods. The ideal-residue-preserving control doubles a coefficient while
  retaining all modulo-ideal residues and both kernel endpoints; its stronger
  valuation obligation correctly fails.

## Reproduce

Python 3.11+; standard library only, from the repository root:

```sh
python -B -I -O research/prime-power-newton-valuation/verify.py --check research/prime-power-newton-valuation/EXPECTED.json
```

Expected: `PASS 214 primitive embeddings; 10268 exact coefficients; 8 negative controls`.
Nine focused tests and the exact [PR 796](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/796) comparison snippet are in the package.

## Pins and verification

- Base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`.
- [PR 621](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/621) head: `520774462b19b29af41554b74def31f9d01e997e`.
- [PR 796](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/796) comparison head: `22902155c7875139e43e4fdf15723142d6709bdd`.
- Kernel source: `openai/math@adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a`.

Normal/isolated optimized replay passes on Windows x86-64, CPython 3.14.7 and
3.12.14; nine tests pass, including optimized changed-receipt and source-drift
rejection. The unchanged [PR 621](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/621) primary replay equals its complete published JSON
receipt. Selected-record/source-inventory integrity passes. A scoped AI proof
worker and separate read-only AI code reviewer found no correctness issue;
the reviewer also checked every coefficient using a descending long-division
reference. No independent human review is claimed.

Only `research/prime-power-newton-valuation/` is added. `upstream/`, the selected
[PR 626](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/626)/[PR 543](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/543) frontier and every existing generator are unchanged. Full `make verify`,
the selected cold supplier replay, Linux and remote CI were not run or claimed;
GNU make is absent on this session's PATH. The scoped checks are complete.

OS-random seed **80**, independent-verification track. No pinned sprint issue
exists; the local claim, three candidates, stopping rule and final overlap are
retained. [PR 796](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/796) was discovered in the submission refresh, and the handoff was
narrowed to distinct divisibility evidence and radix-81 coverage. The final queue
refresh also found [PR 800](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/800)'s unrelated Clifford path valuations, not a kernel overlap.

Prepared for **@navinor** with substantial **Codex assistance**.
Apache-2.0; predecessor and concurrent credits are in NOTICE.md. Written uniform
valuation reasoning and finite replay are not proof-assistant formalization, a
paid inversion/preparation/restoration/tape program, or a full multiplication
theorem. No merge or selected-frontier edit is requested by this contribution.
